title: AI UGC Video Ads for TikTok and Reels | AIVideosUGC
description: Create AI UGC video ads with a casual creator-style look from a product photo. Review the scene, then add captions in TikTok, Reels, or Facebook.
h1: AI UGC Video Ads With a Casual, Creator-Style Look
lead: AI UGC video ads use creator-style visuals made with an AI-generated person. UGC describes the style here, not a real customer review or endorsement.
intro: Creator-style videos use casual handheld framing, everyday light, and a familiar setting. The person and scene are AI-generated, so do not present them as a customer's experience or endorsement.

AIVideosUGC builds this visual style from your product photo and one sentence. Describe the moment you want, then choose 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 and 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Each run creates one AI-generated clip for you to review and edit.

benefits.d: Show one product action, such as a hand opening, lifting, or using the item in a familiar setting.
Skip finding creators and mailing them products. All you need is a clear photo of the item.
Change the first scene in your description and run it again. Each version is a separate video, with its cost shown before it starts.

steps.t: Add a shot of your product
steps.d: A clean shot of the item on its own gives the video an accurate picture of what to put in someone's hand.
Say where it happens and what the hands do, like “unzipping the backpack on a train seat.” Then choose 9:16 and a length.
Save the ad for TikTok or Ads Manager. For a different first second, rewrite the scene and generate a new take.

uses.d: Run the vertical clip as an in-feed ad, adding your captions and music inside TikTok before it goes live.
A casual 9:16 clip fills the Reels placement in Ads Manager with no cropping.
Make a 1:1 version for the feed, where a square video takes up more of the screen than a wide one.
Post the clip on your TikTok or Instagram profile to gauge interest in a product before you spend on ads.

faq.q: What should I write in the description?
faq.a: One everyday moment with your product in it. Name the place, the light, and the action, for example “sunny bathroom counter, hand picks up the soap bar and turns it.” Keep it to a single scene so the clip stays focused.

faq.q: Can I present an AI-generated person as a real customer?
faq.a: No. The person and scene are AI-generated, so do not describe them as a real buyer or add quotes they never gave. Follow the publishing platform's disclosure rules and avoid false endorsements.

faq.q: Can I add captions, a price, or music?
faq.a: Yes, once the clip is downloaded. Captions and music go on in TikTok or CapCut, and prices or discount codes can be added in CapCut or Ads Manager. Typing text yourself avoids the spelling slips that AI-made lettering can have.

overview.h2: Make the first second feel lived in
overview.p: A creator-style ad works when the product enters an ordinary moment: a bag opens, a hand reaches across a desk, or a package is set down before the feature appears. Describe the setting and action plainly so the clip feels like an observation rather than a polished advertising claim.

overview.h2: Keep the visual honest about its source
overview.p: This is an AI-generated product scene, not footage from a real buyer. Use the casual visual language for an ad concept or social post, then add your approved wording and any required AI disclosure in the publishing tool.

input_guide.h2: Set up a believable handheld moment

items.t: Choose an item people can hold
items.d: Bottles, pouches, mugs, phone cases, small bags, and desk accessories give hands a clear relationship to the product.
Use a photo where the silhouette and main color are easy to recognize before the scene adds a room or prop.
A kitchen counter, hallway bench, gym bag, or home office gives the opening a natural context without requiring a long story.
Write “pulls the bottle from the side pocket” or “sets the pouch beside a lunch box,” then stop before adding a second plot.

items.t: Leave the claim for the edit
items.d: Use the generated clip to show the moment; add verified features, prices, and calls to action as typed captions later.
Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds and receive one social-ready visual per run.
Use 9:16 for vertical feeds, 1:1 for square placements, 16:9 for a wide surface, or 4:3 and 3:4 when those crops fit better.
The credit cost is displayed before generation, and failed jobs return the reserved amount.
The download carries no watermark; for commercial-use terms, visit the [FAQ](/faq). Review the claims and labels before publishing.

after_download.h2: Turn the scene into a finished ad

items.t: Add the message in typed text
items.d: Use your editor or ad platform for captions, product names, prices, and dates so small characters remain accurate.
AIVideosUGC does not add voiceover, music, or captions.
If the destination asks for an AI-generated content label, enable it before the post or ad goes live.

items.t: Check that the scene matches reality
items.d: Review hands, product color, packaging, and the action before using the clip in paid media.

fit.h2: Products that suit a creator-style frame
good: Small items that naturally fit in one hand
Everyday goods used at a desk, counter, bench, or entryway
Launches that need several opening scenes to compare
Social ads where a casual visual can sit beside ordinary posts
not_ideal: Products that require an exact spoken explanation or precise on-screen lettering
Claims that depend on a real customer's personal experience
